frequency_question: How often do federal administrative reviews of recognized accrediting bodies result in formal revocation orders rather than renewal or voluntary relinquishment over a multi-year window?
membership_rule: Includes any formal Department of Education review proceeding targeting a recognized national or professional accrediting agency's status where termination or revocation was formally proposed or initiated.

cases.name: American Bar Association accreditation review proceedings resulting in continued recognition
Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools (ACICS) initial termination order
ACICS final termination and loss of federal recognition after appeal
American Bar Association targeted compliance review and continued recognition

coverage_note: 4 prominent contested review processes identified; universe of specialized professional accreditor revocation attempts is extremely small.
known_gaps: Excludes minor advisory committee warnings that did not reach formal department-level termination proceedings.
skeleton: Total formal review cycles of major institutional/professional accreditors by the federal education authority since 2015, categorized by final administrative outcome.
multiplier: 2 revocations out of 4 major contested review cycles in the reference class yields a base frequency.
validity_reason: Regulatory standards and administrative procedures for agency recognition review remain stable across multi-year statutory reauthorization cycles.
